evaluated.name: MarginCollectedInCash
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(RATIO(recch, sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A high operating margin is credible only if the associated revenue is actually collected; margins accompanied by receivable build-up reflect lenient credit terms or channel stuffing and revert, while margins accompanied by receivable liquidation reflect real pricing power.
evaluated.reasoning: The weakest-link MIN is a true conjunction — a firm cannot offset weak collections with a spectacular margin — so the signal is not a log-additive blend of two known anomalies. Scaling both legs by sales makes the accrual leg a revenue-recognition quality measure specific to the margin being tested, rather than a generic asset-scaled accrual.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashConfirmedProfitTurn
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: An improvement in operating profitability is informative only when it is not financed by an expansion of non-cash working capital; margin turns accompanied by receivable and inventory build are accounting-driven and reverse, whereas turns accompanied by shrinking working capital are operationally real.
evaluated.reasoning: Working in first differences of both legs targets the *turn* in profitability rather than its level, which is a distinct question from cash-based operating profitability and less overlapping with the published level anomalies. The MIN conjunction ensures only jointly confirmed improvements populate the long leg, while accrual-financed improvements are pushed to the short leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BookTaxAccrualConcordance
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(txp, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Pretax profitability is credible when the tax authority is being asked to tax it; high book profits unaccompanied by any increase in tax obligations indicate a book-tax gap driven by discretionary accruals rather than by real economic income.
evaluated.reasoning: Tax accounting is a relatively non-discretionary corroborating ledger, so concordance between reported pretax income and accrued tax liabilities is an earnings-quality test that is economically distinct from working-capital accrual measures. This opens a channel none of the archive signals touch, and the MIN conjunction isolates firms where both books agree.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PayablesStretchedCashProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(apalch, sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-backed profitability is itself of varying quality: operating cash flow inflated by stretching payables and accrued liabilities is a borrowed, non-repeatable cash inflow, so high cash margins financed by supplier credit should not earn the cash-profitability premium.
evaluated.reasoning: This inverts the usual framing by questioning the credibility of the cash-flow leg rather than the earnings leg, testing whether the accrual theme adds information even after profits are already measured in cash. Payables expansion is a liability accrual that raises oancf without raising income, so it is exactly the component that contaminates the standard cash-based profitability measure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitPerWorkingCapitalDollar
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality is better captured by the stock of operating capital tied up in receivables and inventory than by its one-year change: a firm that generates a large gross profit per dollar of non-cash current assets converts sales into cash quickly, whereas a firm needing a large accrual base to produce the same profit has earnings that are perpetually at risk of write-down and reversal.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the flow-difference (Sloan) construction entirely — there is no DELTA and no misplaced dlc term — and instead asks how productive the accrual base itself is, so the profitability and accrual themes genuinely multiply rather than one merely deflating the other. Because both numerator and denominator are levels from the same operating cycle, the measure is stable, has near-universal coverage, and is not a monotone re-expression of published accrual anomalies.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitGrowthVsAccrualBaseGrowth
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(revt, cogs), 1)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Growth in profits is durable only when it outpaces growth in the working-capital base that supports it; when receivables and inventory expand faster than gross profit, the reported expansion is being manufactured on the balance sheet and will reverse as those assets are collected at a discount or written down.
evaluated.reasoning: The signal is a congruence (rank-divergence) test between two growth rates rather than a conjunction or a cumulated balance-sheet change, so it neither telescopes into the net-operating-assets anomaly nor repeats the MIN template used elsewhere in the batch. Industry ranking of each growth rate before differencing controls for sector-wide expansion cycles, isolating the firm-specific mismatch between profit growth and accrual-base growth.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WCEfficientProfitNoBaseBuild
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che))), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires both that each dollar of receivables and inventory currently produces a lot of gross profit and that the firm is not expanding that accrual base; efficient-but-expanding working capital signals that current profits are being purchased with future write-downs.
evaluated.reasoning: The two strongest gen-1 results were the level (profit per working-capital dollar) and the flow (profit growth outpacing base growth) versions of the same channel, and this tests whether the level and flow conditions are complementary or redundant. Because MIN requires both, the long leg holds only firms that are efficient today and are not levering up the accrual base to stay that way.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitFreeOfOperatingLiabilityLeverage
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt current liabilities — payables, accrued expenses, deferred items — is financed by stretching suppliers and by deferral accruals, so it is less persistent than the same profitability achieved with a light operating-liability base.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-1 payables idea failed with a cash-flow-statement flow variable (apalch) that halved coverage and proxied for shrinking scale; measuring the operating-liability stock relative to sales on the balance sheet keeps coverage high and captures the standing level of supplier financing rather than a noisy one-year swing. This is the liability-side counterpart to the asset-side working-capital channel and therefore a separable test.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: StableOperatingCycleProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A stable working-capital-to-sales ratio indicates that revenue recognition, collection and inventory policy are disciplined; when that ratio swings year to year the accrual process is noisy and reported margins carry large estimation error, so high margins from unstable operating cycles should not be trusted.
evaluated.reasoning: This measures accrual quality as second-moment instability of the operating cycle rather than as a level or a change, which is a mechanism none of the surviving signals tests. The five-year window costs coverage, so its value must be judged on whether the alpha per unit of coverage exceeds the level-based signals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashBalanceConfirmedProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Real profits eventually show up as a larger cash balance; a firm reporting high operating profitability whose cash stock does not grow is either recycling profits into working capital and receivables or never earned them in cash, and its earnings should revert.
evaluated.reasoning: This corroborates earnings against the cash *stock* on the balance sheet rather than against the cash-flow statement, which is important because every cash-flow-statement leg tested in gen 1 lost half the sample and produced no alpha. The channel is distinct from working-capital intensity: it asks where the profit ended up rather than how much capital it consumed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SupplierFinancedProfitModel
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that are profitable while running negative or minimal net working capital are financed by their customers and suppliers rather than by accrual claims they must later collect; their reported margins are already cash-settled, whereas equally profitable firms carrying large net working capital hold their earnings in receivables and inventory that can still be written down.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a re-parameterization of gross profit per working-capital dollar because the deflator is sales for both legs and the accrual leg is *net* of operating liabilities, so payables enter with a favorable rather than unfavorable sign. It therefore forms a direct competing test against ProfitFreeOfOperatingLiabilityLeverage: if operating-liability financing is a red flag the two signals cannot both work, and whichever wins tells us whether supplier credit is cheap funding or accounting stretch.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LiquidCurrentAssetProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among equally profitable firms, the composition of current assets reveals whether earnings have been realized: a current-asset base dominated by cash means profits are settled, while one dominated by receivables and inventory means the profits are still accounting claims exposed to collection failure, obsolescence and discounting.
evaluated.reasoning: The measure is a stock-composition ratio, not a first difference, so it is not the growth-congruence signal in disguise and it avoids the small, sign-unstable denominator that made the flagged version noisy. It also requires no time-series window, so coverage should match the best gen-1 signals rather than being eroded by lags, and it tests a different question from cash-balance *change*: not whether cash grew, but whether the operating asset base is cash or claims.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NetLiquidCurrentAssetProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only cash that was earned rather than borrowed certifies profitability; netting short-term debt out of the cash balance removes firms whose liquidity is a drawn credit line and keeps firms whose current assets are self-funded settled profits.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic's main objection to the cash leg is that che is confounded by financing, and this is the direct diagnostic: if the gen-2 alpha survives or strengthens after subtracting dlc, the mechanism is earned liquidity, whereas if it collapses the earlier result was a debt-capacity effect. Coverage is unaffected because dlc is a standard balance-sheet item.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeDepreciationCashProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dpc, SUB(at, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms with strong pre-depreciation operating profitability, those charging heavy depreciation against their operating asset base are reporting conservatively — their bottom-line earnings understate cash earning power — and investors who anchor on reported income underprice them.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal has used working-capital accruals; long-term (depreciation) accruals are the other half of total accruals and carry the opposite quality interpretation, since aggressive depreciation depresses rather than inflates income. The risk is that dpc is a cash-flow-statement item with reduced coverage, so this slot is an explicit test of whether the long-term-accrual channel is worth the sample cost.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitGatedLiquidityState
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, act)), INDICATOR(oiadp, 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: Liquidity certifies earnings only when there are earnings to certify: among profitable firms, a cash-dominated current asset base means the reported profits have actually been collected, whereas for loss-making firms the same cash balance carries no information about earnings quality and is merely a burn buffer.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than re-scaling the gen-2 winner, this switches the accrual-composition signal on and off with the profitability state, which is the sharpest possible test of whether the archive's best result is a genuine profitability×accrual interaction or a standalone cash-holdings effect. If the alpha survives with loss firms parked at zero, the interaction is real; if it collapses, the earlier result was liquidity alone and the whole channel needs rethinking.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservatismAdjustedProfitLeanClaims
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Immediate expensing of R&D is the largest conservative accrual in the accounts, so adding it back reveals true economic profitability; firms whose conservatively-understated profits are also generated with a lean receivable-and-inventory base have earnings that are both understated and already converted, the most underpriced combination.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces the intangible-conservatism channel, which no archive signal has touched, and pairs it with operating-cycle leanness measured against sales rather than assets, so it is neither a Novy-Marx rediscovery nor a neighbor of GP/(act−che). COALESCE(xrd, 0) is the economically correct convention because a firm that reports no R&D genuinely has no R&D expensing distortion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithObligationCoveringCash
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, lct)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not the share of current assets held in cash but whether cash covers the claims others hold against the firm; profitable firms whose cash exceeds their current obligations never have to liquidate receivables or inventory at a discount, so their reported profits are not exposed to forced accrual reversal.
evaluated.reasoning: Together with the accepted net-of-debt variant this discriminates among three distinct economic readings of the cash leg — asset realization (che/act), earned versus borrowed liquidity ((che−dlc)/act), and obligation coverage (che/lct) — so whichever wins identifies the true mechanism rather than just re-fitting the winner. All inputs are standard balance-sheet items, so coverage stays at the top of the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithClaimsAtOwnHistoryLow
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Working-capital intensity is a business-model constant, so the informative question is not whether a firm carries more claims than its peers but whether it is carrying more claims than it historically needed for the same sales; profitable firms operating at their own five-year low in claim intensity have genuinely tightened collections and inventory rather than merely belonging to a lean industry.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the low-information smoothing of an already-persistent profitability leg with a firm-specific benchmark on the accrual leg, which removes the mechanical retailer-versus-manufacturer tilt that cross-sectional claim ranks impose. It is a level-in-own-history state, not a first difference, so it should avoid the portfolio instability that killed the alpha of every flow-based leg in the archive while still isolating operational tightening.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitPlusConditionalLiquidityBonus
evaluated.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, act)), INDICATOR(oiadp, 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is priced on its own, and cash realization adds an extra premium only where profits exist; loss firms should receive no liquidity credit because their cash is a burn buffer rather than evidence of collected earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the direct repair of the gen-3 diagnostic: ProfitGatedLiquidityState delivered the archive's best alpha but no FMB slope because it discarded the profitability main effect, while the rank-MIN winners preserve both legs only through the binding constraint. A main-effect-plus-conditional-interaction form should recover the cross-sectional slope and the profit-conditional alpha simultaneously, which is exactly the joint objective.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitScaledDepreciationConservatism
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, ADD(ABS(oibdp), ABS(dpc))), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The share of cash operating profit that management writes off as depreciation measures accounting conservatism in long-term accruals; among cash-profitable firms, those charging a large fraction of EBITDA to depreciation report understated bottom-line earnings and are underpriced by investors who anchor on net income.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-3 long-term-accrual signal worked (alpha 2.7%, fmb 5.2) but the critic correctly noted that dpc/(at−che) proxies for capital intensity and asset age; scaling depreciation by the profit it is charged against removes the asset-base confound and makes the measure a conservatism rate rather than a capital-intensity rate. The bounded denominator keeps the ratio in [-1, 1] so low-EBITDA firms do not explode the tails.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LeanClaimsProfitNoCash
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What certifies profits is the absence of unconverted claims — receivables and inventory — rather than the presence of cash; a profitable firm with a small claim base has already realized its earnings whether or not it chooses to hold the proceeds in cash or reinvest them.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong result so far puts cash in the numerator of the accrual leg, so the alpha may simply be the documented cash-holdings premium among profitable firms; removing cash from the leg entirely and scoring only claim intensity discriminates the two explanations cleanly. If this matches the cash-based versions the mechanism is genuinely accrual realization, and if it fails the archive's leaders need to be reinterpreted and the search redirected toward the depreciation and tax channels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DualAccrualQualityProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, act), RATIO(dpc, ADD(ABS(oibdp), ABS(dpc)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings credibility has two independent accounting sources — short-term realization (current assets already converted to cash) and long-term conservatism (a high share of cash profit charged to depreciation) — and profitability is most durable when it is corroborated on both the working-capital and the fixed-asset side of the accounting system.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of stacking two near-mirror working-capital legs, this averages two accrual-quality channels that are economically and statistically distinct (gen-3 evidence: cash-share alpha 5.8%, depreciation-conservatism alpha 2.7%, driven by different balance-sheet items), so the composite should diversify measurement error rather than merely narrow the sample corner. The averaged accrual score is then required to coincide with genuine profitability through the weakest-link MIN, preserving the conjunctive economics of the archive leaders at essentially unchanged coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LiquidityWeightedProfitCredibility
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual composition determines how much weight investors should place on reported profitability: for a firm whose current assets are cash, the reported profit number is trustworthy and should be extrapolated, while for a claim-heavy firm the same number is a weak signal of underlying economics and should be shrunk toward zero.
evaluated.reasoning: This fixes the defect diagnosed in ProfitGatedLiquidityState — the missing profitability main effect that produced an FMB t of 0.24 — by keeping profitability as the signal and using liquidity as a continuous, non-negative credibility weight rather than a 0/1 gate, so no firm is parked at an artificial mass point. The shrinkage interpretation is a genuine interaction (the slope on profitability varies with accrual quality) rather than a threshold variant, and both legs are high-coverage balance-sheet levels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitableButClaimBloated
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The theory's sharpest prediction concerns the reversal corner: firms showing high gross profitability *together with* a large stock of receivables and inventory are the ones whose reported profits are unconverted claims, and they should subsequently underperform as those claims are collected at a discount or written down.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal has targeted the credible-profits long leg; this is the first construction whose top decile is explicitly the accrual-financed-profits quadrant, so it tests the mechanism on the side where the economic story makes its strongest claim and where mispricing is usually largest. It replaces the discredited book-tax channel with a test that uses only high-coverage balance-sheet levels, and its outcome is informative either way: a reliably negative slope confirms the reversal mechanism, while a null would imply the archive's alphas come from the liquidity long leg alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingProfitLiquidBase
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profit ignores the selling and administrative cost of generating sales, and firms that book high gross margins only by spending heavily on distribution have less durable earnings; operating profitability net of SG&A should therefore interact more cleanly with cash realization.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong archive result uses the same gross-profit numerator, so the profitability definition has never been tested against the realization leg even though the accounting literature treats operating profitability as the more persistent measure. This isolates the numerator choice with everything else held fixed, and because xsga is widely reported the coverage cost should be small.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LiquidProfitPlusAssetScaledConservatism
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, act), RATIO(dpc, SUB(at, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Short-term realization and long-term depreciation conservatism are independent accounting corroborations of the same profits, and averaging them yields a broader earnings-quality score than either alone; profitability that clears this combined quality bar is the most durable.
evaluated.reasoning: DualAccrualQualityProfit produced the archive's largest alpha (6.3%) but a dead FMB slope and a poor Sharpe, and the likely culprit is the profit-scaled depreciation leg that separately failed at −0.7% alpha; swapping in the asset-scaled depreciation leg that earned +2.7% keeps the dual-channel idea while removing the term that mechanically fights the profitability rank. If the FMB slope and Sharpe recover while the alpha stays near 6%, this becomes the strongest joint-evidence signal in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NetWorkingCapitalClaimsProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically correct accrual stock is net of what suppliers and accrued expenses finance: a firm whose receivables and inventory are funded by payables has no unconverted claim exposure of its own, so profitability should be judged against *net* rather than gross working capital.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested gross claims (worked, 4.2% alpha) and operating liabilities alone (failed, −1.1%), but never the netted stock at level, even though it is the standard balance-sheet accrual definition and the gen-1 *change* version of exactly this quantity delivered a 2.9% alpha with the best Sharpe in that generation. The comparison directly answers whether payables should be credited or ignored when assessing earnings credibility, and coverage is unaffected.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithClaimsAtOwnHistoryHigh
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Reported profits are least durable when a firm is simultaneously highly profitable and carrying more receivables and inventory per sales dollar than at any point in its own recent history — the configuration in which current earnings have been pulled forward onto the balance sheet and must reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-4 cross-sectional reversal-corner test worked but only modestly (−2.2% alpha), plausibly because cross-sectional claim intensity is dominated by industry business models; benchmarking each firm against its own five-year history isolates genuine stretching, and that same own-history normalization improved the long-side signal in gen 3. It is the archive's only short-side mechanism, so strengthening it materially widens the spread available to the overall strategy rather than re-fitting the crowded long leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ClaimsAgainstEquityCushion
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), ceq))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Unconverted claims are dangerous in proportion to the equity that must absorb their write-down: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory are small relative to book equity can take a collection or obsolescence loss without impairing shareholders, whereas one whose claims are a multiple of equity has profits that are one write-down away from disappearing.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg tested so far deflates claims by assets, sales, or the firm's own history; benchmarking them against the equity cushion introduces a solvency-of-accruals mechanism rather than an intensity mechanism, which is why the same firm can look lean on assets and exposed on equity. The profitability leg is left untouched so the cross-sectional slope that the archive shows lives in that leg is preserved, and both inputs are high-coverage balance-sheet levels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DebtFundedClaimsProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, SUB(act, che)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not only how large the claim base is but who funds it: receivables and inventory carried on short-term borrowings must be liquidated on the lender's schedule, so profits resting on debt-financed claims are fragile, while the same claims funded internally can be held to maturity and collected in full.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested the size of the claim base, its liquidity counterpart, and its change, but never its funding source, and the gen-3 result that netting dlc out of cash left the alpha intact suggests short-term debt carries information that has not yet been used in the right place. Pairing funding fragility of the accrual base with clean gross profitability keeps the FMB-bearing leg intact while adding a genuinely new portfolio tilt away from revolver-financed inventory businesses.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualPerClaimDollarProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(act, che)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The classic income-minus-cash-flow accrual is most damaging when it is large relative to the claim base that must eventually convert it; profitable firms whose accruals are small per dollar of receivables and inventory are running an accounting system that turns claims into cash rather than one that keeps recycling them.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has never tested the canonical earnings-minus-cash-flow accrual at all — every accrual leg so far is balance-sheet composition — and deflating it by the claim stock rather than by assets makes it a conversion-failure rate rather than a size-scaled accrual, which is the form that matches the economic story. The oancf requirement will cut coverage relative to the pure balance-sheet signals, so this slot explicitly prices whether the canonical accrual is worth its sample cost.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashProfitLiquidBase
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the mechanism is truly that profits must be cash-backed, then measuring the profitability leg in cash flow rather than in accounting margin should strengthen the conjunction, because a cash-flow margin already embeds the accrual adjustment that the realization leg is trying to verify.
evaluated.reasoning: All strong archive results use an accrual-based profitability numerator paired with a balance-sheet realization leg, so we have never asked whether cash-flow profitability and cash composition are complements or the same information counted twice. A materially higher alpha would say the two are complementary evidence; a materially lower one would say the realization leg has already extracted the cash-backing information, which is directly useful for the final consolidation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RisingCashConversionProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(che, act), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose current asset base has been steadily shifting from claims into cash over five years is progressively converting reported profits into settled value, and that multi-year direction of travel is evidence about earnings quality that a single-year change cannot provide.
evaluated.reasoning: One-year changes in the cash balance failed (alpha −0.4%) because they are dominated by financing and timing noise, but a five-year trend is a slow-moving state rather than a noisy flow, which is precisely the distinction that made the own-history claim-intensity signal work in gen 3. This tests whether the realization channel has a dynamic dimension at all, at a modest coverage cost.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TripleEvidenceCredibilityScore
evaluated.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, act)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(dpc, SUB(at, che)))), INDICATOR(oiadp, 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is the priced characteristic, and both short-term realization and long-term depreciation conservatism are corroborating evidence whose value applies only to firms that actually report operating profits; adding them as a profit-conditional bonus preserves the pricing of profitability while capturing the quality tilt.
evaluated.reasoning: The two constructions that reached the archive's highest alphas (7.2% and 6.3%) both buried the profitability leg inside a composite and lost the FMB slope, whereas the gen-4 additive gated form kept a live slope (3.99) at 5.8% alpha — this applies that structural fix to the richer two-channel quality score. It is the most direct attempt in the archive to hold both forms of evidence simultaneously rather than trading one for the other, and it uses only variables whose coverage is already proven.

evaluated.name: CashFlowCoveredClaimsProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Claims are safe when the business generates enough operating cash each year to fund them: a profitable firm whose annual operating cash flow is large relative to its outstanding receivables and inventory never depends on collecting those claims to stay solvent, whereas one whose claim stock dwarfs its cash generation must realize every accrual at book value or take a loss.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's realization legs all measure a cash *stock* (che scaled by various denominators), which the critic rightly notes are monotone cousins of each other; this replaces the stock with the cash *flow* that services the claim base, a genuinely different quantity that can be high for firms holding little cash and low for cash hoards with bloated inventories. It therefore discriminates the "hoarding" interpretation of the archive's leaders from the "conversion capacity" interpretation, at the coverage cost of requiring oancf.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConsistentProfitLiquidBase
evaluated.expression: MIN(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(oiadp, 0), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durability of profits has two components — their current magnitude and the number of past years in which the firm actually earned an operating profit — and cash realization certifies the combination; a firm that has been profitable in all five years and holds its current assets in cash has earnings that are neither cyclical nor accrual-manufactured.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike a moving average of an already-persistent ratio, a count of profitable years is not a smoothed version of the profitability level — it separates firms with identical current margins but very different track records, which is precisely the "durable versus about to reverse" distinction the task targets and which no archive signal measures. Pairing this durability score with the best-performing realization leg keeps the conjunctive structure that has carried both the FMB slope and the alpha, at the modest coverage cost of a five-year history.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ClaimEfficientProfitLowAccruals
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Two conditions make profits durable: each dollar of unconverted claims must generate a lot of gross profit, and each dollar of sales must come with little accrual accounting; the sales deflator prices accruals against the revenue that generated them rather than against a claim stock that can vanish for cash-rich firms.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the deflator instability the critic identified in AccrualPerClaimDollarProfit — where act−che approaches zero the ratio explodes and produces spurious top ranks — by moving the fragile denominator to the profitability leg, where it is a well-behaved efficiency measure that already earned a 4.9% alpha on its own. The two legs now use different deflators, so the conjunction is not dominated by a single unstable quantity.

evaluated.name: ChronicAccrualUserProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), TS_SUM(sale, 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Single-year accruals reverse and therefore mismeasure earnings quality; a firm that has cumulated positive accruals over three consecutive years per dollar of cumulative sales is systematically running earnings ahead of cash, and that chronic pattern — not one year's timing difference — is what predicts reversal.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual literature's central mechanical fact is that accruals mean-revert within a year or two, so cumulating them over three years isolates the non-reversing component that indicates a persistent accounting policy rather than a working-capital swing. This is a horizon test on the archive's highest-Sharpe channel and is distinct from the one-year version rather than a rescaling of it, since the cumulative measure nets out reversals that the annual measure counts twice.

evaluated.name: LiquidityAndNetClaimExposureProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, act), NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash realization and net claim exposure are economically distinct — one says profits have been converted, the other says the firm's own capital is not tied up in unconverted claims after crediting supplier financing — so a firm strong on both has the most credible earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the collinear che/act and che/lct pair the critic rejected, these two legs have different numerators, different signs on payables, and independently strong records (5.8% alpha with FMB 5.30, and 4.2% alpha with FMB 5.86), so averaging them tests complementarity rather than rehashing one proxy. It also avoids the failure mode of the depreciation composites, whose orthogonal capital-intensity leg destroyed the FMB slope, because both legs here carry strong slopes of their own.

evaluated.name: CashProfitNetClaimExposure
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: When profitability is already measured in cash, the informative accrual dimension is not how much cash the firm holds but how much of its capital is still locked in net unconverted claims; cash margin plus low net claim exposure identifies businesses whose cash generation is structural rather than a working-capital release.
evaluated.reasoning: CashProfitLiquidBase (cash margin paired with cash share) delivered 6.6% alpha and 0.51 Sharpe, but its two legs both key on cash and may double-count, whereas pairing cash margin with the net claim stock asks whether the accrual leg still adds information once profitability is cash-based. The answer directly determines which pairing the final generations should consolidate on.

evaluated.name: ProductionCycleClaimsProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), cogs))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Claims should be benchmarked against the cost of the goods that created them: inventory is carried at cost and receivables arise from cost-incurring production, so claims per dollar of cost of goods sold measures the physical length of the operating cycle, and profitable firms with short cost-cycles convert output into cash before the accounting can drift from the economics.
evaluated.reasoning: Every claim-intensity leg in the archive is deflated by assets, sales, equity, or the firm's own history, and each deflator implies a different economic question; the cost deflator is the one that maps to physical throughput rather than to pricing power or capital structure, and it is unaffected by the margin differences that make sales-deflated claims mechanically low for high-margin firms. It uses only full-coverage income-statement and balance-sheet items, so unlike the withdrawn COALESCE construction its economic meaning is constant across the whole sample.

evaluated.name: BalanceSheetAccrualPerClaimProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), SUB(act, che)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The share of the current claim base that was newly created this year measures how fast a firm is manufacturing accruals relative to the claims it already carries; profitable firms adding little to an existing claim stock are converting output, while those whose claim base is mostly new are recognizing revenue ahead of collection.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best Sharpe (0.63) came from deflating the accrual by the claim stock rather than by assets, but that construction needs oancf and therefore only 8% coverage; this builds the same accrual-per-claim rate from balance-sheet items available for the full sample. It also differs from the failed asset-scaled accrual-change legs precisely in the deflator that the evidence identifies as the source of the efficiency gain, so it isolates deflator versus data source.

evaluated.name: CashVerifiedEarningsReversal
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear highly profitable while their income exceeds operating cash flow by a large fraction of their outstanding claims are recognizing earnings they have not collected, and those earnings should reverse with negative abnormal returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the gen-7 proposal that failed validation for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable by restoring the claim-stock deflator, which is also the deflator that produced the archive's best risk-adjusted long-side performance. The archive's short-side evidence is its weakest element (−2.2% and −0.1% alpha from balance-sheet corners), and testing the condemned corner with the better-measured accrual determines whether the mechanism is symmetric or purely a long-side quality premium.

evaluated.name: NetAccrualStabilityProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose net accrual position swings sharply from year to year is running an accounting system with large estimation error, so its reported profitability is a noisy signal of economics regardless of the current accrual level; stable accrual positions certify that reported profits track collections.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's only instability test used gross claims scaled by sales with a margin leg and was weak (1.4% alpha, t=1.58), but the net accrual stock is the theoretically correct object and gross profitability has proven the stronger partner leg, so this is a genuine second look at the accrual-quality (second-moment) mechanism rather than a repeat. It is the batch's distinct-mechanism slot and carries only a modest coverage cost since all inputs are balance-sheet items.

evaluated.name: ClaimTurnoverProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings are credible when the claim base recycles quickly: a firm that runs many dollars of sales through each dollar of receivables and inventory collects and reships before accounting estimates can drift, whereas slow-turning claims accumulate collection, obsolescence and valuation risk regardless of how much cash the firm happens to hold.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the saturated cash-numerator realization leg with claim *velocity*, a characteristic that is not rank-collinear with che/act or che/lct — a low-cash, fast-turning distributor and a cash-rich, slow-turning manufacturer sit at opposite ends of this leg and the same end of the cash legs. It is also not the archived GP/(act−che), since that ratio mixes margin with turnover while this conjunction requires asset-level profitability and claim velocity separately, and it uses only full-coverage items.

evaluated.name: SupplierFundedClaimShareProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: When a profitable firm's receivables and inventory are financed by payables and accrued expenses rather than by its own capital, none of the firm's own money is exposed to those unconverted claims, so a write-down falls on suppliers' terms rather than on shareholders' equity.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's liability evidence is currently contradictory — operating liabilities scaled by sales failed (−1.1% alpha) while netting them out of the claim stock worked (+4.2%, FMB 5.86) — and the funding-share ratio resolves the contradiction by measuring what fraction of claims suppliers actually carry rather than the size of either side. It is a differently ordered characteristic from net working capital because it is scale-free in the claim base, so large lean firms and small claim-heavy firms are ranked by funding structure rather than by claim magnitude.

evaluated.name: GrossProfitCashConversionLeanClaims
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, SUB(revt, cogs))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The sharpest cash-backing test is what fraction of the gross profit a firm books actually arrives as operating cash; a high conversion rate combined with a small stock of outstanding claims identifies firms whose margins are settled rather than promised.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the flagged pairing, the two legs here are not driven by a common term — the conversion rate is a cash-flow-to-income-statement ratio while the claim leg is a pure balance-sheet stock — so the conjunction combines genuinely independent evidence about the same construct. The conversion-rate characteristic itself is new to the archive, which has deflated oancf only by sales, assets, or the claim stock, never by the profit it is supposed to validate.

evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two facts that most strongly certify earnings are that each dollar of unconverted claims produces a lot of gross profit and that what the firm does hold in current assets is cash; together they describe a business that converts output quickly and keeps the proceeds.

Because the profitability leg is deflated by claims and the accrual leg by current assets, the conjunction is not a monotone transform of either parent and should raise alpha without the slope dilution that averaging causes.

evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), cogs)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The operating cash conversion cycle — days of claims carried against sales minus days of supplier credit carried against cost — is the accounting system's own measure of how long reported profits remain unsettled; profitable firms with short or negative cycles collect before their estimates can drift.

It is a genuinely different characteristic from the netted stock because a high-margin firm and a low-margin firm with identical net working capital have very different cycle lengths.

evaluated.name: OperatingAssetProfitSupplierFunded
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(at, che))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The durable configuration is a firm that earns a high return on the assets it actually operates — excluding the idle cash balance that dilutes measured productivity — while financing its receivables and inventory with supplier credit rather than its own capital, so neither its profits nor its balance sheet depend on collecting unconverted claims.
evaluated.reasoning: Neither leg in this pairing has been evaluated together, and the profitability leg is new to the archive entirely: measuring gross profit against non-cash assets asks about operating productivity rather than about total capital, which changes the ranking of cash-rich firms in the opposite direction from the cash-share legs. Combining it with the leg carrying the archive's strongest cross-sectional slope (FMB 5.72) targets exactly the metric where the pure cash-leg conjunctions are weakest, at unchanged full coverage.

evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durability of profits is a property of their time series, not only of their level: a firm whose gross profitability has been steady for five years and whose current assets are held in cash has earnings that are both economically stable and already collected, whereas volatile profitability signals that the reported number is a draw from a wide distribution regardless of accrual composition.

This is a genuinely different characteristic from the additive gated template the critic rejected, and its five-year window costs about the same coverage as the archive's other volatility signals.

evaluated.name: EbitdaProfitLiquidBase
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating income before depreciation is the profitability measure closest to cash earnings, since it excludes the single largest non-cash accrual in the income statement; pairing it with cash realization should give the cleanest possible reading of profits that are both economically real and already collected.

This isolates the last untested profitability numerator against the archive's benchmark accrual leg at full coverage, which is the right way to close out the consolidation.

evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Each firm reveals its true working-capital requirement through the leanest claims-per-sales ratio it has achieved in recent years; carrying claims well above that self-revealed floor is operational slack — uncollected receivables and unsold inventory — rather than the capital the business needs, and profits accompanied by such slack are less durable.

It remains distinct from the archive's TS_RANK own-history signal because the benchmark is the achieved floor rather than the distribution position, which matters for firms whose claim intensity has drifted persistently in one direction.

considered.name: AccrualPenalizedROA
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ib, ABS(SUB(ib, oancf))), at)
considered.hypothesis: Reported ROA should be discounted by the absolute size of the accrual wedge, regardless of its sign, because large accrual magnitudes (in either direction) signal discretionary or transitory accounting content in earnings.
considered.reasoning: Two firms with identical ROA are ranked differently according to how much of that ROA is accounting rather than cash, which is a genuine interaction rather than a linear combination of ROA and signed accruals. The absolute-value penalty captures accrual reliability (estimation intensity) instead of only the well-known negative signed-accrual effect.

considered.name: CashGatedOperatingProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)), INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, ib), 0))
considered.hypothesis: The operating-profitability premium exists only in the subsample where operating cash flow exceeds accounting income; for firms whose earnings exceed cash generation, high reported profitability carries no incremental information about future returns.
considered.reasoning: The indicator switches the profitability signal on only for cash-confirmed firms, making the payoff explicitly state-dependent rather than an additive blend of two themes. Industry z-scoring of profitability removes sector-level margin differences so that the gate isolates within-industry accounting credibility.

considered.name: SustainedProfitNoAccrualSpike
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires that a firm has not needed a single large accrual accumulation in recent years; the worst accrual year, not the average, reveals when reported profits were manufactured.
considered.reasoning: Averaging accruals lets a large one-off accrual spike be masked by later reversals, so the maximum over three years is the sharper measure of accounting stretch, and interacting it with smoothed profitability separates repeatedly cash-generative firms from serial accrual users. The temporal transformation is required because "durability" and "one-off manipulation" are inherently multi-period concepts.

considered.name: AccrualNoiseDiscountedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality is better measured by the instability of the accrual process (Dechow-Dichev style) than by its level; profitable firms with noisy accruals have earnings dominated by estimation error and should command lower future returns than equally profitable firms with stable accruals.
considered.reasoning: Volatility of scaled accruals proxies for the unreliability of the mapping from earnings to cash, so it grades the credibility of a given profitability level rather than repeating the signed-accrual anomaly. The conjunctive rank product ensures only high-profitability, low-accrual-noise firms load on the long leg.

considered.name: CashConfirmedProfitTurn
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm's improvement in operating profitability is informative only if it is accompanied by a simultaneous decline in accrual intensity; margin gains delivered while accruals expand are accounting-driven and reverse, whereas margin gains delivered with shrinking accruals reflect genuine operating cash generation.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the rank product with a weakest-link MIN makes the conjunction genuinely non-additive: a firm scores high only if it clears both hurdles, and a superb score on one dimension cannot compensate for a poor score on the other. Working in first differences of both profitability and accruals moves the signal away from cash-based profitability levels toward the distinct question of whether a profitability *turn* is cash-confirmed or accrual-financed.

considered.name: AccrualShareOfProfit
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(ABS(oibdp), ABS(SUB(ib, oancf)))), 1)
considered.hypothesis: What matters is not the dollar size of accruals relative to assets but the fraction of a firm's profit engine that is accrual rather than cash; the same accrual dollar is far more suspicious for a marginally profitable firm than for a highly profitable one, so accrual share of operating profit predicts earnings reversal better than asset-scaled accruals.
considered.reasoning: Scaling accruals by operating profitability rather than by assets makes the profitability theme enter the denominator, so the signal is an explicit interaction in which accrual quality is measured per unit of earnings power instead of per unit of capital. Adding the absolute accrual term to the denominator bounds the ratio in [-1, 1], removing the small-denominator blowups that make profit-scaled ratios unstable and preserving broad coverage without discarding low-profit firms.

considered.name: MarginCollectedInCash
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), IND_RANK(RATIO(recch, sale)))
considered.hypothesis: A high operating margin is credible only if the associated revenue is actually collected; margins accompanied by receivable build-up reflect lenient credit terms or channel stuffing and revert, while margins accompanied by receivable liquidation reflect real pricing power.
considered.reasoning: The weakest-link MIN is a true conjunction — a firm cannot offset weak collections with a spectacular margin — so the signal is not a log-additive blend of two known anomalies. Scaling both legs by sales makes the accrual leg a revenue-recognition quality measure specific to the margin being tested, rather than a generic asset-scaled accrual.

considered.name: CashConfirmedProfitTurn
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: An improvement in operating profitability is informative only when it is not financed by an expansion of non-cash working capital; margin turns accompanied by receivable and inventory build are accounting-driven and reverse, whereas turns accompanied by shrinking working capital are operationally real.
considered.reasoning: Working in first differences of both legs targets the *turn* in profitability rather than its level, which is a distinct question from cash-based operating profitability and less overlapping with the published level anomalies. The MIN conjunction ensures only jointly confirmed improvements populate the long leg, while accrual-financed improvements are pushed to the short leg.

considered.name: BookTaxAccrualConcordance
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(txp, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Pretax profitability is credible when the tax authority is being asked to tax it; high book profits unaccompanied by any increase in tax obligations indicate a book-tax gap driven by discretionary accruals rather than by real economic income.
considered.reasoning: Tax accounting is a relatively non-discretionary corroborating ledger, so concordance between reported pretax income and accrued tax liabilities is an earnings-quality test that is economically distinct from working-capital accrual measures. This opens a channel none of the archive signals touch, and the MIN conjunction isolates firms where both books agree.

considered.name: PayablesStretchedCashProfit
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(apalch, sale))))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-backed profitability is itself of varying quality: operating cash flow inflated by stretching payables and accrued liabilities is a borrowed, non-repeatable cash inflow, so high cash margins financed by supplier credit should not earn the cash-profitability premium.
considered.reasoning: This inverts the usual framing by questioning the credibility of the cash-flow leg rather than the earnings leg, testing whether the accrual theme adds information even after profits are already measured in cash. Payables expansion is a liability accrual that raises oancf without raising income, so it is exactly the component that contaminates the standard cash-based profitability measure.

considered.name: GrossProfitPerWorkingCapitalDollar
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality is better captured by the stock of operating capital tied up in receivables and inventory than by its one-year change: a firm that generates a large gross profit per dollar of non-cash current assets converts sales into cash quickly, whereas a firm needing a large accrual base to produce the same profit has earnings that are perpetually at risk of write-down and reversal.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the flow-difference (Sloan) construction entirely — there is no DELTA and no misplaced dlc term — and instead asks how productive the accrual base itself is, so the profitability and accrual themes genuinely multiply rather than one merely deflating the other. Because both numerator and denominator are levels from the same operating cycle, the measure is stable, has near-universal coverage, and is not a monotone re-expression of published accrual anomalies.

considered.name: ProfitGrowthVsAccrualBaseGrowth
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(revt, cogs), 1)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Growth in profits is durable only when it outpaces growth in the working-capital base that supports it; when receivables and inventory expand faster than gross profit, the reported expansion is being manufactured on the balance sheet and will reverse as those assets are collected at a discount or written down.
considered.reasoning: The signal is a congruence (rank-divergence) test between two growth rates rather than a conjunction or a cumulated balance-sheet change, so it neither telescopes into the net-operating-assets anomaly nor repeats the MIN template used elsewhere in the batch. Industry ranking of each growth rate before differencing controls for sector-wide expansion cycles, isolating the firm-specific mismatch between profit growth and accrual-base growth.

considered.name: WCEfficientProfitNoBaseBuild
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(act, che))), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires both that each dollar of receivables and inventory currently produces a lot of gross profit and that the firm is not expanding that accrual base; efficient-but-expanding working capital signals that current profits are being purchased with future write-downs.
considered.reasoning: The two strongest gen-1 results were the level (profit per working-capital dollar) and the flow (profit growth outpacing base growth) versions of the same channel, and this tests whether the level and flow conditions are complementary or redundant. considered.name: ProfitFreeOfOperatingLiabilityLeverage
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt current liabilities — payables, accrued expenses, deferred items — is financed by stretching suppliers and by deferral accruals, so it is less persistent than the same profitability achieved with a light operating-liability base.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 payables idea failed with a cash-flow-statement flow variable (apalch) that halved coverage and proxied for shrinking scale; measuring the operating-liability stock relative to sales on the balance sheet keeps coverage high and captures the standing level of supplier financing rather than a noisy one-year swing. This is the liability-side counterpart to the asset-side working-capital channel and therefore a separable test.
